title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
claim: Training decomposes into two stages: self-supervised pretext tasks build image-generation skills, then task-specific tuning applies them to graded reasoning levels.
layout: 2 stacked colored bands, top-to-bottom stage order, left-to-right arrows, image thumbnails
description: The figure has two stacked, color-coded bands, with a tall gray arrow down the left edge to show the order. The top blue band, 'Stage 1: Pretext Reasoning', walks through a Jigsaw example from left to right. A corrupted shuffled-tile image leads to a quoted grounded-text description, then to the restored image, then to a second quoted description. Below it, a row of seven small before→after thumbnail pairs shows pretext transformations: colorization, super-resolution, inpainting, rotation/flip, denoising and deformation recovery. The bottom pink band, 'Stage 2: Task-specific Interleaved Instruction Tuning', has three rounded boxes joined by arrows: L1 Basic Visual Perception, L2 Static Spatial Understanding and L3 Mental World Modeling. Under each box is an example input→output image pair. The eye goes first to the large stage titles and the photographs.
caption: Overview of the two training stages. Stage 1 (top) uses seven instruction-free visual pretext tasks to practice producing and reading intermediate images. Stage 2 (bottom) uses question-driven instruction tuning to teach the model to use image content to advance reasoning across basic visual perception, static spatial understanding, and mental world modeling.
abstract: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corrupted or transformed image, generate a restored or canonical image, and interpret the result. The second stage uses automatically constructed demonstrations for question-driven instruction tuning. At the same instruction-tuning budget, models trained with pretext reasoning outperform those trained with instruction tuning alone. The full recipe improves over the base model by an average of 11.33 accuracy points across twelve benchmarks. These results show that supervision derived from images can build the visual skills needed for interleaved reasoning and improve learning from task-specific demonstrations.
